catalog_quote: II Initial main stress, no info on sec stress: ... Nyamal (T79): Inferred from: word lists Tindale (1953), Geytenbeek, Ms, AIATSIS, Canberra. [Appendix D introduction:] This is a list of languages categorised by stress type and annotated with the main descriptive source and some codes denoting special characteristics of the stress pattern in that language. ... Some of the entries have no descriptive source. These must be handled with caution. The stress pattern in these languages was deduced from old scanty material found in the Australian Institute for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies (AIATSIS) library and at the Australian National University (ANU). It may be that some of them have been mistakenly placed in a certain category, due to missing crucial information. Yet, they were included for completeness sake.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand database classification only: StressTyp (Goedemans 1998) files Nyamal under 'initial main stress', explicitly INFERRED from word lists (Tindale 1953; Geytenbeek MS) rather than from any description; no primary source states a Nyamal stress rule. Every opened primary/bibliographic source (Thieberger 1993 handbook, von Brandenstein 1967, AUSTLANG A58, Oates 1975, Wangka Maya pages and brochures, Glottolog's 30 refs) is silent on Nyamal stress; no grammar, sketch or phonology of Nyamal exists.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; inferred from wordlist citation forms. StressTyp2 (live 2026-09-17) no longer carries a Nyamal record (0 of 699). Thieberger 1993 intro has only the areal remark 'Word stress is usually on the first syllable' for WA languages generally, not Nyamal-specific.
new_statements.identity_note: Nyamal proper (nyam1271, AUSTLANG A58, ISO nly). Two named varieties: Punyju/'heavy'/High Nyamal (western, coastal) and Wirtakarri/Witukari/'light'/Low Nyamal (eastern, Marble Bar; AUSTLANG A60 Witukari, Bundjuwanga A75 per Oates). The Goedemans 1998 inference is not tied to a variety. Note AUSTLANG W40 is Ngarla (ngar1286), not Nyamal — the code used in one earlier download was wrong and that file was removed.
